title: Loyalty points tested on real PostgreSQL
scenario: Tests on H2 passed; production PostgreSQL rejected the upsert the code relied on.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · @SpringBootTest · Testcontainers with @ServiceConnection and disabledWithoutDocker · PostgreSQL 17 upsert (ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING) · H2 (trap test only) · JdbcClient · Flyway
simulation: Customers, orders and points are demo data, not Basketo's. Points are rows in a ledger; no shop or payment system calls in. The earning rate is a demo rule.

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. Green on H2

    Basketo's loyalty tests ran on H2, in PostgreSQL mode. The upsert, written in H2's MERGE ... KEY syntax, passed every test.

  2. Red in production

    The first customer to earn points after the release got an error: PostgreSQL does not know that syntax. Nobody's points were saved until a hotfix.

  3. The fix

    Write the upsert PostgreSQL understands, and run every test against a real PostgreSQL 17 in Docker, the same version as production.

A test proves something only about the database it ran on. Test on the one you ship to.

What are we building?

Customers earn points on orders (POST /loyalty/{id}/earn) and spend them (POST /loyalty/{id}/redeem). Every change is a ledger entry plus an atomic change of the balance, and every test runs on real PostgreSQL.

An everyday analogy

A driving test in a simulator that lets you drive on the left and the right. You pass; then the real road only allows one. H2 in PostgreSQL mode is the simulator: friendly, fast, and not the road.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. The tests start PostgreSQL 17 in Docker; Spring connects to it (@ServiceConnection).
  2. Flyway creates the real schema, constraints and all.
  3. Each test makes its own customers, so it never depends on another test's data.
  4. Without Docker, the tests are skipped, and say so: never passed, never failed.
Check yourself: why not keep H2 for speed and add a few PostgreSQL tests?

Because every query is a chance for a dialect difference, and you do not know in advance which ones. The shared PostgreSQL container starts once per run; after that, tests are about as fast.

What this station is not

  • No order system. Earn is called directly.
  • No expiry or tiers. Points stay.
  • No history endpoint. That is challenge 1.

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Basketo (a fictional grocery chain) shipped loyalty code whose only tests ran on H2. PostgreSQL rejected its upsert in production.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Given a customer with no points earns on a ₹1,499 order, then 201, 14 points, and the balance row is created.
  2. Given another order, then the points are added to the same row; an order under ₹100 earns 0.
  3. Given the same order again, in any case, then 409 and the balance is unchanged.
  4. Given 20 earns at once for a new customer, then all 20 are counted.
  5. Given a redemption above the balance, then 422; an unknown customer, 404; a malformed body, 400.
  6. Given Docker is not running, then the tests are reported as skipped.

Requirements

  • Every test runs on the database version production runs.
  • No test depends on data another test created.
  • Balances never go below zero; an order earns once; both enforced by the database.
  • The ledger entry and the balance change commit together.

Learning objectives

  • Write @SpringBootTest tests against a real database with Testcontainers and @ServiceConnection.
  • Keep tests independent of each other's data.
  • Write PostgreSQL's upsert and know why it is safe under concurrency.
  • Choose a strategy for machines without Docker that never lies.

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Testing on H2 and shipping SQL that PostgreSQL rejects.

The trap test runs the old upsert, MERGE INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) KEY (customer_id) VALUES (?, ?), in two places. On in-memory H2 in PostgreSQL mode it works: the old suite was green. On PostgreSQL 17 it is a syntax error at the column list, because PostgreSQL's MERGE is the SQL-standard one (MERGE INTO t USING …). The third test turns it around: H2 cannot even parse the upsert PostgreSQL needs, so code that is right for production could never have been tested on H2.

While building, each part was undone once. Putting the old MERGE back turned 5 tests red; an upsert that replaces the balance instead of adding to it, 2 (including the 20-at-once test); a redemption without the points >= ? condition, 1.

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.DriverManager;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.sql.Statement;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

/**
 * The first test written for this station. The old upsert, from the code that shipped, run on the in-memory H2 the
 * old tests used (even in its PostgreSQL compatibility mode it accepts H2's own syntax), and on the real PostgreSQL
 * production runs.
 */
class H2VersusPostgresTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    /** H2's own MERGE syntax (a column list and a KEY clause): not SQL standard, not PostgreSQL. */
    static final String OLD_UPSERT = "MERGE INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) KEY (customer_id) VALUES (?, ?)";

    static final String NEW_UPSERT = """
            INSERT INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) VALUES (?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET points = point_balances.points + EXCLUDED.points RETURNING points""";

    static Connection h2() throws SQLException {
        Connection c = DriverManager.getConnection("jdbc:h2:mem:old-tests;MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE");
        try (Statement s = c.createStatement()) {
            s.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS point_balances (customer_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, points INT NOT NULL)");
        }
        return c;
    }

    @Test
    void theOldUpsertRunsOnH2() throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = h2(); var merge = c.prepareStatement(OLD_UPSERT)) {
            merge.setLong(1, 7);
            merge.setInt(2, 14);
            assertThat(merge.executeUpdate()).isEqualTo(1);   // green on H2: the old test suite passed
        }
    }

    @Test
    void andPostgresqlRejectsIt() {
        long customer = newCustomer();
        // PostgreSQL has a standard MERGE (MERGE INTO t USING ...), so it stops at the column list H2 allowed.
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql(OLD_UPSERT).params(customer, 14).update())
                .rootCause().hasMessageContaining("syntax error at or near \"(\"");   // the first production earn after the release
    }

    @Test
    void theRightSqlForPostgresqlIsNotH2Sql() throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = h2()) {
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> c.prepareStatement(NEW_UPSERT)).isInstanceOf(SQLException.class)
                    .hasMessageContaining("Syntax error");   // H2 cannot even parse it: it can only be tested on PostgreSQL
        }
        long customer = newCustomer();
        assertThat(jdbc.sql(NEW_UPSERT).params(customer, 14).query(Integer.class).single()).isEqualTo(14);
    }
}

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ResponseStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.Locale;

@RestController
class LoyaltyController {

    /** Demo limits: an order up to ₹10 lakh; up to 100,000 points redeemed at once. */
    record Earn(@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[A-Za-z0-9-]{4,30}") String orderRef, @NotNull @Min(1) @Max(100_000_000) Long amountPaise) {
    }

    record Redeem(@NotNull @Min(1) @Max(100_000) Integer points) {
    }

    private final LoyaltyLedger ledger;

    LoyaltyController(LoyaltyLedger ledger) {
        this.ledger = ledger;
    }

    /** Demo: unprotected. In a shop, only the order system may call earn, after the order is paid. */
    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/earn")
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
    LoyaltyLedger.Earned earn(@PathVariable long customerId, @Valid @RequestBody Earn body) {
        return ledger.earn(customerId, body.orderRef().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), body.amountPaise());
    }

    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/redeem")
    LoyaltyLedger.Redeemed redeem(@PathVariable long customerId, @Valid @RequestBody Redeem body) {
        return ledger.redeem(customerId, body.points());
    }
}

src/main/java/com/basketo/loyalty/LoyaltyLedger.java

Does
Ledger entry plus balance change, in one transaction.
Why
PostgreSQL's upsert: atomic, even for a customer's first points arriving twice at once.
Without it
Lost or doubled points.
  • ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET points = point_balances.points + EXCLUDED.points adds, it does not replace.
  • RETURNING points gives the new balance without a second query.
  • Redeem is UPDATE ... WHERE points >= ?: no row means not enough.
package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

/**
 * Points earned and redeemed. Each change is a ledger entry plus an atomic change of the balance row, in one
 * transaction. Demo rule: 1 point per full ₹100 spent.
 */
@Service
class LoyaltyLedger {

    record Earned(long customerId, String orderRef, int earned, int balance) {
    }

    record Redeemed(long customerId, int redeemed, int balance) {
    }

    static final long PAISE_PER_POINT = 10_000;

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;

    LoyaltyLedger(JdbcClient jdbc) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
    }

    @Transactional
    Earned earn(long customerId, String orderRef, long amountPaise) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        int points = (int) (amountPaise / PAISE_PER_POINT);
        try {
            jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, order_ref, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'EARN')").params(customerId, orderRef, points).update();
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Already earned", "Order " + orderRef + " already earned points for customer " + customerId + ".");
        }
        // PostgreSQL's upsert: insert the balance row, or add to it, in one atomic statement. Not valid H2, and that is fine:
        // the tests run on PostgreSQL.
        int balance = jdbc.sql("""
                INSERT INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) VALUES (?, ?)
                ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET points = point_balances.points + EXCLUDED.points
                RETURNING points""").params(customerId, points).query(Integer.class).single();
        return new Earned(customerId, orderRef, points, balance);
    }

    @Transactional
    Redeemed redeem(long customerId, int points) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        Integer balance = jdbc.sql("UPDATE point_balances SET points = points - ? WHERE customer_id = ? AND points >= ? RETURNING points")
                .params(points, customerId, points).query(Integer.class).optional().orElse(null);
        if (balance == null) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Not enough points", "Customer " + customerId + " has fewer than " + points + " points.");
        }
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, 'REDEEM')").params(customerId, -points).update();
        return new Redeemed(customerId, points, balance);
    }

    private void requireCustomer(long id) {
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE id = ?").param(id).query(Long.class).single() == 0) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Customer not found", "No customer " + id + ".");
        }
    }

    static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__customers_points.sql

Customers, balances and the ledger, with named constraints.

-- Basketo loyalty: a ledger of every change, and one balance row per customer kept in step with it.
CREATE TABLE customers (
    id   BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE point_balances (
    customer_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    points      INT NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT point_balances_customer_fk FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id),
    CONSTRAINT point_balances_not_negative CHECK (points >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE point_entries (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    order_ref   VARCHAR(30),
    delta       INT         NOT NULL,
    reason      VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_customer_fk FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id),
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_reason_known CHECK (reason IN ('EARN', 'REDEEM')),
    -- An earn has an order and adds (an order under ₹100 adds 0); a redemption has no order and takes away.
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_sign_matches CHECK ((reason = 'EARN' AND order_ref IS NOT NULL AND delta >= 0) OR (reason = 'REDEEM' AND order_ref IS NULL AND delta < 0)),
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_order_once UNIQUE (customer_id, order_ref)
);

src/test/java/com/basketo/loyalty/H2VersusPostgresTrapTest.java

Written first: the old upsert on H2 and on PostgreSQL, and the new one on both.

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.DriverManager;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.sql.Statement;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

/**
 * The first test written for this station. The old upsert, from the code that shipped, run on the in-memory H2 the
 * old tests used (even in its PostgreSQL compatibility mode it accepts H2's own syntax), and on the real PostgreSQL
 * production runs.
 */
class H2VersusPostgresTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    /** H2's own MERGE syntax (a column list and a KEY clause): not SQL standard, not PostgreSQL. */
    static final String OLD_UPSERT = "MERGE INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) KEY (customer_id) VALUES (?, ?)";

    static final String NEW_UPSERT = """
            INSERT INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) VALUES (?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET points = point_balances.points + EXCLUDED.points RETURNING points""";

    static Connection h2() throws SQLException {
        Connection c = DriverManager.getConnection("jdbc:h2:mem:old-tests;MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE");
        try (Statement s = c.createStatement()) {
            s.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS point_balances (customer_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, points INT NOT NULL)");
        }
        return c;
    }

    @Test
    void theOldUpsertRunsOnH2() throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = h2(); var merge = c.prepareStatement(OLD_UPSERT)) {
            merge.setLong(1, 7);
            merge.setInt(2, 14);
            assertThat(merge.executeUpdate()).isEqualTo(1);   // green on H2: the old test suite passed
        }
    }

    @Test
    void andPostgresqlRejectsIt() {
        long customer = newCustomer();
        // PostgreSQL has a standard MERGE (MERGE INTO t USING ...), so it stops at the column list H2 allowed.
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql(OLD_UPSERT).params(customer, 14).update())
                .rootCause().hasMessageContaining("syntax error at or near \"(\"");   // the first production earn after the release
    }

    @Test
    void theRightSqlForPostgresqlIsNotH2Sql() throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = h2()) {
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> c.prepareStatement(NEW_UPSERT)).isInstanceOf(SQLException.class)
                    .hasMessageContaining("Syntax error");   // H2 cannot even parse it: it can only be tested on PostgreSQL
        }
        long customer = newCustomer();
        assertThat(jdbc.sql(NEW_UPSERT).params(customer, 14).query(Integer.class).single()).isEqualTo(14);
    }
}

Named constraints, a rollback of both rows, and 20 earns at once.

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

/** The tables' rules with Java bypassed, a rollback of both rows, and the upsert under concurrency. */
class LoyaltyDatabaseTest extends ApiTest {

    @Autowired
    LoyaltyLedger ledger;
    @Autowired
    TransactionTemplate transaction;

    @Test
    void namedConstraintsHoldWithoutJava() {
        long c = newCustomer();
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) VALUES (?, 5)").param(c).update();
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql("UPDATE point_balances SET points = -1 WHERE customer_id = ?").param(c).update()).hasMessageContaining("point_balances_not_negative");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) VALUES (999999, 1)").update()).hasMessageContaining("point_balances_customer_fk");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, delta, reason) VALUES (?, 5, 'EARN')").param(c).update()).hasMessageContaining("point_entries_sign_matches");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, delta, reason) VALUES (?, 5, 'REDEEM')").param(c).update()).hasMessageContaining("point_entries_sign_matches");
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, order_ref, delta, reason) VALUES (?, 'BK-1', 5, 'EARN')").param(c).update();
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, order_ref, delta, reason) VALUES (?, 'BK-1', 5, 'EARN')").param(c).update())
                .hasMessageContaining("point_entries_order_once");
    }

    @Test
    void anEarnThatFailsAfterItsWritesLeavesNeither() {
        long c = newCustomer();
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> transaction.executeWithoutResult(s -> {
            ledger.earn(c, "BK-6001", 500_000);   // joins this transaction: entry and balance written...
            throw new IllegalStateException("the order system called back: payment failed");
        })).hasMessageContaining("payment failed");
        assertThat(balance(c)).isNull();   // ...and both rolled back
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM point_entries WHERE customer_id = ?").param(c).query(Long.class).single()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void twentyEarnsAtOnceForANewCustomerAddUp() throws Exception {
        long c = newCustomer();   // no balance row yet: twenty requests race to create it
        AtomicInteger order = new AtomicInteger();
        List<Integer> statuses = together(20, () -> earn(c, "BK-7" + order.incrementAndGet(), 100_000).andReturn().getResponse().getStatus());
        assertThat(statuses).containsOnly(201);
        assertThat(balance(c)).isEqualTo(200);   // 20 orders x 10 points: the upsert never lost one
    }
}

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.ResultActions;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.Callable;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
import java.util.concurrent.Future;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;

import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;

/**
 * Shared setup: the whole app (@SpringBootTest) on a real PostgreSQL 17 (@ServiceConnection in PostgresTestConfig).
 * Without Docker, every test here is SKIPPED with that reason, never failed and never passed.
 * Isolation: each test makes its own customers, so no test depends on another's data or on the order they run in.
 */
@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureMockMvc
@Import(PostgresTestConfig.class)
@Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true)
abstract class ApiTest {

    private static final AtomicLong NEXT_CUSTOMER = new AtomicLong(1000);

    @Autowired
    MockMvc mvc;
    @Autowired
    JdbcClient jdbc;

    /** A customer no other test knows about, with no points yet. */
    long newCustomer() {
        long id = NEXT_CUSTOMER.incrementAndGet();
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO customers (id, name) VALUES (?, 'Test customer ' || ?)").params(id, id).update();
        return id;
    }

    ResultActions earn(long customer, String orderRef, long paise) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(post("/loyalty/{id}/earn", customer).contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                .content("{\"orderRef\":\"%s\",\"amountPaise\":%d}".formatted(orderRef, paise)));
    }

    ResultActions redeem(long customer, int points) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(post("/loyalty/{id}/redeem", customer).contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content("{\"points\":" + points + "}"));
    }

    Integer balance(long customer) {
        return jdbc.sql("SELECT points FROM point_balances WHERE customer_id = ?").param(customer).query(Integer.class).optional().orElse(null);
    }

    /** Runs n copies of the task on virtual threads, all released together by one latch. */
    static <T> List<T> together(int n, Callable<T> task) throws Exception {
        CountDownLatch start = new CountDownLatch(1);
        List<Future<T>> futures = new ArrayList<>();
        try (ExecutorService threads = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                futures.add(threads.submit(() -> {
                    start.await();
                    return task.call();
                }));
            }
            start.countDown();
        }
        List<T> results = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Future<T> f : futures) {
            results.add(f.get());
        }
        return results;
    }
}

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

import java.util.List;

/**
 * Points earned and redeemed. Each change is a ledger entry plus an atomic change of the balance row, in one
 * transaction. Demo rule: 1 point per full ₹100 spent.
 */
@Service
class LoyaltyLedger {

    record Earned(long customerId, String orderRef, int earned, int balance) {
    }

    record Redeemed(long customerId, int redeemed, int balance) {
    }

    record Entry(String reason, int delta, String orderRef) {
    }

    record Statement(long customerId, int balance, List<Entry> entries) {
    }

    record Reversed(long customerId, String orderRef, int reversed, int balance) {
    }

    static final long PAISE_PER_POINT = 10_000;

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;

    LoyaltyLedger(JdbcClient jdbc) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
    }

    @Transactional
    Earned earn(long customerId, String orderRef, long amountPaise) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        int points = (int) (amountPaise / PAISE_PER_POINT);
        try {
            jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, order_ref, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'EARN')").params(customerId, orderRef, points).update();
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Already earned", "Order " + orderRef + " already earned points for customer " + customerId + ".");
        }
        // PostgreSQL's upsert: insert the balance row, or add to it, in one atomic statement. Not valid H2, and that is fine:
        // the tests run on PostgreSQL.
        int balance = jdbc.sql("""
                INSERT INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) VALUES (?, ?)
                ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET points = point_balances.points + EXCLUDED.points
                RETURNING points""").params(customerId, points).query(Integer.class).single();
        return new Earned(customerId, orderRef, points, balance);
    }

    @Transactional
    Redeemed redeem(long customerId, int points) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        Integer balance = jdbc.sql("UPDATE point_balances SET points = points - ? WHERE customer_id = ? AND points >= ? RETURNING points")
                .params(points, customerId, points).query(Integer.class).optional().orElse(null);
        if (balance == null) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Not enough points", "Customer " + customerId + " has fewer than " + points + " points.");
        }
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, 'REDEEM')").params(customerId, -points).update();
        return new Redeemed(customerId, points, balance);
    }

    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    Statement statement(long customerId) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        int balance = jdbc.sql("SELECT coalesce((SELECT points FROM point_balances WHERE customer_id = ?), 0)").param(customerId).query(Integer.class).single();
        List<Entry> entries = jdbc.sql("SELECT reason, delta, order_ref FROM point_entries WHERE customer_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC").param(customerId).query(Entry.class).list();
        return new Statement(customerId, balance, entries);
    }

    /** Takes back an order's points once, only if they are still there: a balance never goes below zero. */
    @Transactional
    Reversed reverse(long customerId, String orderRef) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        int earned = jdbc.sql("SELECT delta FROM point_entries WHERE customer_id = ? AND order_ref = ? AND reason = 'EARN'").params(customerId, orderRef)
                .query(Integer.class).optional()
                .orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Order not found", "Order " + orderRef + " earned no points for customer " + customerId + "."));
        try {
            jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, order_ref, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'REVERSE')").params(customerId, orderRef, -earned).update();
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Already reversed", "Order " + orderRef + " was already reversed.");
        }
        Integer balance = jdbc.sql("UPDATE point_balances SET points = points - ? WHERE customer_id = ? AND points >= ? RETURNING points")
                .params(earned, customerId, earned).query(Integer.class).optional().orElse(null);
        if (balance == null) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Points already spent", "Order " + orderRef + "'s " + earned + " points were already redeemed.");
        }
        return new Reversed(customerId, orderRef, earned, balance);
    }

    private void requireCustomer(long id) {
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE id = ?").param(id).query(Long.class).single() == 0) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Customer not found", "No customer " + id + ".");
        }
    }

    static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;

import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;

import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ResponseStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.Locale;

@RestController
class LoyaltyController {

    /** Demo limits: an order up to ₹10 lakh; up to 100,000 points redeemed at once. */
    record Earn(@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[A-Za-z0-9-]{4,30}") String orderRef, @NotNull @Min(1) @Max(100_000_000) Long amountPaise) {
    }

    record Redeem(@NotNull @Min(1) @Max(100_000) Integer points) {
    }

    private final LoyaltyLedger ledger;

    LoyaltyController(LoyaltyLedger ledger) {
        this.ledger = ledger;
    }

    /** Demo: unprotected. In a shop, only the order system may call earn, after the order is paid. */
    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/earn")
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
    LoyaltyLedger.Earned earn(@PathVariable long customerId, @Valid @RequestBody Earn body) {
        return ledger.earn(customerId, body.orderRef().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), body.amountPaise());
    }

    @GetMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}")
    LoyaltyLedger.Statement statement(@PathVariable long customerId) {
        return ledger.statement(customerId);
    }

    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/earn/{orderRef}/reversal")
    LoyaltyLedger.Reversed reverse(@PathVariable long customerId, @PathVariable String orderRef) {
        return ledger.reverse(customerId, orderRef.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
    }

    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/redeem")
    LoyaltyLedger.Redeemed redeem(@PathVariable long customerId, @Valid @RequestBody Redeem body) {
        return ledger.redeem(customerId, body.points());
    }
}

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/**
 * Challenge 2: POST /loyalty/{customerId}/earn/{orderRef}/reversal takes back the points an order earned (the order
 * was returned), as a REVERSE ledger entry, once. Points already spent: 409, nothing changes. Unknown order: 404.
 * The schema must allow the new entry (a migration).
 */
class ReversalChallengeTest extends ApiTest {

    @Test
    void aReturnedOrderGivesItsPointsBackOnce() throws Exception {
        long c = newCustomer();
        earn(c, "BK-9001", 500_000);   // 50
        earn(c, "BK-9002", 200_000);   // 20
        mvc.perform(post("/loyalty/{id}/earn/{order}/reversal", c, "bk-9002")).andExpect(status().isOk()).andExpect(jsonPath("$.balance").value(50));
        mvc.perform(post("/loyalty/{id}/earn/{order}/reversal", c, "BK-9002")).andExpect(status().isConflict());
        redeem(c, 45);
        mvc.perform(post("/loyalty/{id}/earn/{order}/reversal", c, "BK-9001")).andExpect(status().isConflict())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.title").value("Points already spent"));
        assertThat(balance(c)).isEqualTo(5);
        mvc.perform(post("/loyalty/{id}/earn/{order}/reversal", c, "BK-0000")).andExpect(status().isNotFound());
    }
}

-- Challenge 2: an earn can be reversed once; the reversal names the same order.
ALTER TABLE point_entries DROP CONSTRAINT point_entries_reason_known;
ALTER TABLE point_entries ADD CONSTRAINT point_entries_reason_known CHECK (reason IN ('EARN', 'REDEEM', 'REVERSE'));
ALTER TABLE point_entries DROP CONSTRAINT point_entries_sign_matches;
ALTER TABLE point_entries ADD CONSTRAINT point_entries_sign_matches CHECK (
    (reason = 'EARN' AND order_ref IS NOT NULL AND delta >= 0)
    OR (reason = 'REDEEM' AND order_ref IS NULL AND delta < 0)
    OR (reason = 'REVERSE' AND order_ref IS NOT NULL AND delta <= 0));
ALTER TABLE point_entries DROP CONSTRAINT point_entries_order_once;
ALTER TABLE point_entries ADD CONSTRAINT point_entries_order_once UNIQUE (customer_id, order_ref, reason);

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import org.springframework.dao.DuplicateKeyException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

import java.util.List;

/**
 * Points earned and redeemed. Each change is a ledger entry plus an atomic change of the balance row, in one
 * transaction. Demo rule: 1 point per full ₹100 spent.
 */
@Service
class LoyaltyLedger {

    record Earned(long customerId, String orderRef, int earned, int balance) {
    }

    record Redeemed(long customerId, int redeemed, int balance) {
    }

    record Entry(String reason, int delta, String orderRef) {
    }

    record Statement(long customerId, int balance, List<Entry> entries) {
    }

    record Reversed(long customerId, String orderRef, int reversed, int balance) {
    }

    static final long PAISE_PER_POINT = 10_000;

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;

    LoyaltyLedger(JdbcClient jdbc) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
    }

    @Transactional
    Earned earn(long customerId, String orderRef, long amountPaise) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        int points = (int) (amountPaise / PAISE_PER_POINT);
        try {
            jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, order_ref, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'EARN')").params(customerId, orderRef, points).update();
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Already earned", "Order " + orderRef + " already earned points for customer " + customerId + ".");
        }
        // PostgreSQL's upsert: insert the balance row, or add to it, in one atomic statement. Not valid H2, and that is fine:
        // the tests run on PostgreSQL.
        int balance = jdbc.sql("""
                INSERT INTO point_balances (customer_id, points) VALUES (?, ?)
                ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET points = point_balances.points + EXCLUDED.points
                RETURNING points""").params(customerId, points).query(Integer.class).single();
        return new Earned(customerId, orderRef, points, balance);
    }

    @Transactional
    Redeemed redeem(long customerId, int points) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        Integer balance = jdbc.sql("UPDATE point_balances SET points = points - ? WHERE customer_id = ? AND points >= ? RETURNING points")
                .params(points, customerId, points).query(Integer.class).optional().orElse(null);
        if (balance == null) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Not enough points", "Customer " + customerId + " has fewer than " + points + " points.");
        }
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, 'REDEEM')").params(customerId, -points).update();
        return new Redeemed(customerId, points, balance);
    }

    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    Statement statement(long customerId) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        int balance = jdbc.sql("SELECT coalesce((SELECT points FROM point_balances WHERE customer_id = ?), 0)").param(customerId).query(Integer.class).single();
        List<Entry> entries = jdbc.sql("SELECT reason, delta, order_ref FROM point_entries WHERE customer_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC").param(customerId).query(Entry.class).list();
        return new Statement(customerId, balance, entries);
    }

    /** Takes back an order's points once, only if they are still there: a balance never goes below zero. */
    @Transactional
    Reversed reverse(long customerId, String orderRef) {
        requireCustomer(customerId);
        int earned = jdbc.sql("SELECT delta FROM point_entries WHERE customer_id = ? AND order_ref = ? AND reason = 'EARN'").params(customerId, orderRef)
                .query(Integer.class).optional()
                .orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Order not found", "Order " + orderRef + " earned no points for customer " + customerId + "."));
        try {
            jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO point_entries (customer_id, order_ref, delta, reason) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'REVERSE')").params(customerId, orderRef, -earned).update();
        } catch (DuplicateKeyException e) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Already reversed", "Order " + orderRef + " was already reversed.");
        }
        Integer balance = jdbc.sql("UPDATE point_balances SET points = points - ? WHERE customer_id = ? AND points >= ? RETURNING points")
                .params(earned, customerId, earned).query(Integer.class).optional().orElse(null);
        if (balance == null) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Points already spent", "Order " + orderRef + "'s " + earned + " points were already redeemed.");
        }
        return new Reversed(customerId, orderRef, earned, balance);
    }

    private void requireCustomer(long id) {
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE id = ?").param(id).query(Long.class).single() == 0) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Customer not found", "No customer " + id + ".");
        }
    }

    static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

package com.basketo.loyalty;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ResponseStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.Locale;

@RestController
class LoyaltyController {

    /** Demo limits: an order up to ₹10 lakh; up to 100,000 points redeemed at once. */
    record Earn(@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[A-Za-z0-9-]{4,30}") String orderRef, @NotNull @Min(1) @Max(100_000_000) Long amountPaise) {
    }

    record Redeem(@NotNull @Min(1) @Max(100_000) Integer points) {
    }

    private final LoyaltyLedger ledger;

    LoyaltyController(LoyaltyLedger ledger) {
        this.ledger = ledger;
    }

    /** Demo: unprotected. In a shop, only the order system may call earn, after the order is paid. */
    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/earn")
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
    LoyaltyLedger.Earned earn(@PathVariable long customerId, @Valid @RequestBody Earn body) {
        return ledger.earn(customerId, body.orderRef().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), body.amountPaise());
    }

    @GetMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}")
    LoyaltyLedger.Statement statement(@PathVariable long customerId) {
        return ledger.statement(customerId);
    }

    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/earn/{orderRef}/reversal")
    LoyaltyLedger.Reversed reverse(@PathVariable long customerId, @PathVariable String orderRef) {
        return ledger.reverse(customerId, orderRef.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
    }

    @PostMapping("/loyalty/{customerId}/redeem")
    LoyaltyLedger.Redeemed redeem(@PathVariable long customerId, @Valid @RequestBody Redeem body) {
        return ledger.redeem(customerId, body.points());
    }
}

Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test: the old SQL on H2 and on PostgreSQL.
  2. Move every test to a shared PostgreSQL container with @ServiceConnection.
  3. Make each test create its own data.
  4. Write PostgreSQL's upsert, and test it under concurrency.

Design alternatives and trade-offs

ApproachWhat it costsVerdict
Testcontainers with production's PostgreSQL versionDocker on every machine and in CI; a few seconds to start.Chosen
H2 in compatibility modeFast; accepts SQL production rejects, rejects SQL production needs.The trap
A shared test database on a serverTests collide with each other and with people.No
Embedded PostgreSQL binaries (no Docker)Real PostgreSQL; one more tool to keep at the right version.If Docker is impossible
Clean tables before each testSimple; tests cannot run in parallel.Fine for small suites

Database design

TableConstraints
point_balancespoint_balances_customer_fk, point_balances_not_negative
point_entriespoint_entries_customer_fk, point_entries_reason_known, point_entries_sign_matches, point_entries_order_once
-- Basketo loyalty: a ledger of every change, and one balance row per customer kept in step with it.
CREATE TABLE customers (
    id   BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE point_balances (
    customer_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    points      INT NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT point_balances_customer_fk FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id),
    CONSTRAINT point_balances_not_negative CHECK (points >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE point_entries (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    order_ref   VARCHAR(30),
    delta       INT         NOT NULL,
    reason      VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_customer_fk FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id),
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_reason_known CHECK (reason IN ('EARN', 'REDEEM')),
    -- An earn has an order and adds (an order under ₹100 adds 0); a redemption has no order and takes away.
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_sign_matches CHECK ((reason = 'EARN' AND order_ref IS NOT NULL AND delta >= 0) OR (reason = 'REDEEM' AND order_ref IS NULL AND delta < 0)),
    CONSTRAINT point_entries_order_once UNIQUE (customer_id, order_ref)
);

A Foundations station: the considerations to know, no runbook.

CI must not go green on skips
Skipping without Docker is honest on a laptop. In CI it would turn "no tests ran" into a green build. Make CI fail when tests were skipped, or when Docker is missing.
Same version
Pin the container image to production's major version (here postgres:17-alpine) and upgrade both together.
Speed
One container per run, shared by every test, keeps the cost to a few seconds. Reusable containers can keep it across runs on a developer machine.
Upsert and sequences
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE still uses up identity values on conflict; gaps in ids are normal.

Interview takeaways

Why not test with H2?

Because H2 is not the database you ship to. Its compatibility modes accept syntax production rejects and lack features production has, so green tests prove little about production SQL.

What does @ServiceConnection do?

It turns a container bean into Spring's connection details: the datasource URL, user and password come from the running container, with no properties to write.

How do you keep tests independent?

Each test creates its own data (fresh ids) or resets what it uses, and never relies on the order tests run in.

What happens when Docker is missing?

With @Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true), the tests are skipped and reported as skipped. Without it, they fail. Neither is a pass.

Why is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE safe under concurrency?

PostgreSQL resolves the conflict with the unique index inside one statement: concurrent upserts for the same key wait for each other and then update, instead of both inserting or one failing.

This Foundations station has no flawed version to review. Use this checklist on any test suite with a database:

  • Which database, and which version, do the tests run on?
  • Does any test need another test's data, or a particular order?
